name: Time-series momentum, sign of past return (long/short)
author: Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen
summary: Go long if the asset's past 12-month excess return is positive, short if negative; the original TSMOM paper finds strong persistence for 1-12 month lookbacks across 58 futures.
notes: Original is on futures, rebalanced monthly with 40% vol-scaled positions; here daily re-evaluation, no vol scaling, excess over T-bill ignored. Applied to BTC per this catalogue.

name: Absolute momentum long/cash vs T-bill (Antonacci)
author: Gary Antonacci
summary: Hold the risky asset when its 12-month return exceeds the T-bill return, otherwise cash; claims drawdowns cut sharply while keeping most of the return.
notes: T-bill proxied by us2y (annual %, pro-rated to the lookback). Original lookback 12 months on equities with monthly checks; daily here.

name: Dual momentum BTC vs ETH (BTC leg)
author: Gary Antonacci
summary: Dual momentum: pick the stronger of two risky assets by relative momentum and hold it only if its absolute momentum is positive; here BTC is held when it beats ETH and its own lookback return is positive.
notes: Antonacci's GEM uses US/intl equities + bonds with 12-month lookback, monthly. Pair with mom-dual-btc-eth-ethleg to form the full switch; cash hurdle simplified to zero.

name: Dual momentum BTC vs ETH (ETH leg)
author: Gary Antonacci
summary: ETH leg of the BTC/ETH dual-momentum switch: hold ETH when it outperformed BTC over the lookback and its own lookback return is positive.
notes: Mirror of the BTC leg; together they hold the stronger coin or cash. Original book is equity/bond based.

name: Century of trend: 1/3/12-month majority vote
author: Hurst, Ooi, Pedersen
summary: Equal-weight combination of 1-, 3- and 12-month time-series momentum signals; positive in every decade since 1880 per AQR.
long_entry: ((close > shift(close, 21)) & (close > shift(close, 63))) | ((close > shift(close, 21)) & (close > shift(close, 252))) | ((close > shift(close, 63)) & (close > shift(close, 252)))
long_exit: ((close < shift(close, 21)) & (close < shift(close, 63))) | ((close < shift(close, 21)) & (close < shift(close, 252))) | ((close < shift(close, 63)) & (close < shift(close, 252)))
short_entry: ((close < shift(close, 21)) & (close < shift(close, 63))) | ((close < shift(close, 21)) & (close < shift(close, 252))) | ((close < shift(close, 63)) & (close < shift(close, 252)))
short_exit: ((close > shift(close, 21)) & (close > shift(close, 63))) | ((close > shift(close, 21)) & (close > shift(close, 252))) | ((close > shift(close, 63)) & (close > shift(close, 252)))
notes: Original averages the three signals (fractional positions) with vol scaling; approximated as a 2-of-3 majority vote at full size.

name: Two centuries of trend: price vs EMA
author: Lemperiere, Deremble, Seager, Potters, Bouchaud
summary: Signal is the sign of price minus its exponential moving average (about 5-month time scale); trend premium found stable over two centuries across asset classes.
notes: Paper normalises the signal by volatility and uses a continuous position; here sign only. n=100 is the ~5 month default.

name: Liu-Tsyvinski weekly time-series momentum (top quintile)
author: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Strong time-series momentum in crypto: BTC next-week return is ~11% after a top-quintile week vs ~2.6% after a bottom-quintile week.
notes: Paper sorts weekly returns into quintiles and holds one week; top quintile approximated by z-score of the 7-day return above 0.84 (normal top 20%). Weekly rebalancing not expressible; exit when weekly return falls below its mean.

name: Liu-Tsyvinski short-horizon intrinsic momentum
author: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Daily and weekly crypto returns positively predict the following day/week returns for BTC, ETH and XRP (intrinsic momentum).
notes: Paper reports predictive regressions and quintile sorts; long-only sign-of-return rule at 1-7 day horizons is the simplest trading translation. ETH effect reported weaker.

name: Detzel et al. price-to-moving-average ratio rule
author: Detzel, Liu, Strauss, Zhou, Zhu
summary: Ratios of BTC price to its 5-100 day moving averages forecast daily returns; hold BTC above the SMA, T-bills below; higher Sharpe and smaller drawdowns than buy-and-hold.
notes: Financial Management 2021 (WP 'Bitcoin: Predictability and Profitability via Technical Analysis', 2018). SMAs 5,10,20,50,100; gross Sharpe 2.6 (5d) to 2.2 (100d) 2010-2017.

name: Hong Bitcoin time-series momentum 1-8 weeks
author: Kihoon Hong
summary: Bitcoin returns persist for 1-8 weeks then partly reverse; a weekly TSMOM strategy on BTC combined with S&P momentum improves return per unit risk.
notes: Weekly returns and weekly holding in the paper; lookbacks of 1-8 weeks expressed in days with daily evaluation.

name: Catching Crypto Trends: Donchian with midpoint trailing stop
author: Carlo Zarattini, Alberto Pagani, Andrea Barbon
summary: Long-only: enter when close breaks the n-day max close, exit on a trailing stop at the channel midpoint; nine lookbacks 5-360 days ensembled with a 25% vol target; Sharpe > 1.5 net on top-20 coins.
notes: Original ensembles lookbacks 5,10,20,30,60,90,150,250,360 equally with vol-target sizing (25%/90d stdev, cap 2x) and a ratcheting stop (max of prior stop and midpoint); here one lookback at a time, non-ratcheting midpoint exit, full size. SSRN 5209907 / SFI RP 25-80.

name: Bitcoin MAX: hold at n-day high
author: Matus Padysak, Radovan Vojtko
summary: Hold BTC the day after it closes at its n-day maximum; strong momentum after local maxima, best at 10-20 days.
notes: Paper holds while BTC is at its x-day max (one-day holding re-checked daily); lookbacks 10-50 tested.

name: Bitcoin MAX+MIN combined
author: Matus Padysak, Radovan Vojtko
summary: Hold BTC when it is at either its n-day maximum (trend) or n-day minimum (mean reversion), flat otherwise; original reported 98% annual return with -38% max drawdown 2015-2022.
notes: Combined 10-day best in original; Quantpedia's 2024 revisit found the MIN leg weak recently and MAX 20-day stronger than 10-day.

name: ETH momentum after positive abnormal day
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: After a one-day abnormal return, crypto prices keep moving in the same direction the next day (momentum), except BTC after positive and ETH after negative shocks.
long_entry: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
long_exit: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
notes: Abnormal day = return beyond mean +/- k sd of a rolling window; hold one day. Paper's same-day intraday hourly momentum is not expressible on daily bars.

name: BTC short after negative abnormal day
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: For BTC the next-day momentum after abnormal days holds for negative shocks: short BTC for one day after an abnormally negative day.
short_entry: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
short_exit: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
notes: One-day holding; paper found contrarian (not momentum) behaviour for BTC after positive abnormal days, so only the short side is taken.

name: Catching Crypto Trends: long-short Donchian (appendix)
author: Carlo Zarattini, Alberto Pagani, Andrea Barbon
summary: Long-short extension of the BTC Donchian model: short on a break below the n-day min close, cover on a midpoint trailing stop; BTC combo Sharpe 1.31 (2015-2025, gross) vs 1.58 long-only.
notes: Paper Table 5: BTC long-short Sharpe 1.05 (5d), 1.15 (20d), 1.04 (360d). Ratcheting stop and 25% vol target not expressed; midpoint used as a fixed exit.

name: Gerritsen et al. trading range breakout
author: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud
summary: Buy when BTC breaks above its n-day high, sell when it breaks below its n-day low; the only rule of seven to beat buy-and-hold on a bootstrapped Sharpe basis (2010-2019).
notes: Finance Research Letters 34 (2020). Same n for entry and exit as in the paper; Sharpe advantage concentrated in strong trending years (2011-12, 2013-14, 2017-18). No costs.

name: Gerritsen et al. moving-average rules (1/50, 2/150, 5/200)
author: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud
summary: Classic Brock-Lakonishok-LeBaron MA rules on daily BTC: long while the short MA is above the long MA; mixed results versus buy-and-hold.
notes: Pairs tested in the paper are (1,50), (2,150), (5,200); grid here includes other combos. Source page is a TradingView summary of the FRL paper (DOI 10.1016/j.frl.2019.08.011). Same rule shape as Rozario et al. 2020 (arXiv 2009.12155), who found a 10/40-day SMA pair consistently good on BTC with walk-forward re-optimisation (255% annualised 2011-2019, costs ignored).

name: Gerritsen et al. MACD zero-line rule
author: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud
summary: Buy BTC when the MACD line (12/26 EMA difference) is above zero, sell when below; significant outperformance only in one variant.
notes: Paper also examines signal-line and histogram variants without stated settings.

name: Gerritsen et al. rate-of-change rule
author: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud
summary: Buy BTC when the price is above its level n days ago (ROC > 0), sell when below; one of seven trend rules tested on 2010-2019 daily BTC.
notes: n=10 is the stated common default; long/cash interpretation.

name: Gerritsen et al. on-balance-volume MA crossover
author: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud
summary: Buy BTC when a short MA of on-balance volume crosses above a long MA of OBV, sell on the reverse cross.
notes: MA lengths not given in the summary; assumed the paper's price-MA pairs. OBV computed on USD turnover here.

name: Hudson-Urquhart filter rule
author: Robert Hudson, Andrew Urquhart
summary: Alexander filter rule from the ~15,000-rule universe: buy after price rises x% above its recent low, sell after it falls x% below its recent high; predictability found in all crypto rule classes, breakeven costs well above actual costs.
notes: Sullivan-Timmermann-White filter universe uses x from 0.5% to 50% and an extremum window; window fixed at 20 days here. Accepted version notes no out-of-sample BTC predictability.

name: Hudson-Urquhart channel breakout
author: Robert Hudson, Andrew Urquhart
summary: Channel breakout: when the n-day high-low channel is narrower than x%, buy on a close above the channel top; sell on a close below the channel bottom.
long_entry: (highest(close, n, 1) < lowest(close, n, 1) * (1 + x)) & (close > highest(close, n, 1))
notes: STW channel rule with fixed holding period c days; exit at channel bottom substituted for the fixed holding period.

name: Hudson-Urquhart MA rule with band
author: Robert Hudson, Andrew Urquhart
summary: Moving-average class from the STW universe: long when the short MA exceeds the long MA by more than a b% band, exit when it falls below by b%.
notes: Paper finds predictability for every class and coin, with ETH among the other cryptocurrencies that keep out-of-sample predictability; specific best rules not stated in abstract.

name: Corbet et al. variable-length MA with 1% band
author: Corbet, Eraslan, Lucey, Sensoy
summary: VMA rule: long whenever the short MA is more than a band above the long MA, short when more than a band below; best rule in the study, buy signals stronger than sells.
notes: Original runs on 1-minute BTC bars (short 1-10 min, long 5-200 min); translated to daily bars with the classic Brock et al. lengths. Exit at the plain cross is a simplification.

name: Corbet et al. trading range breakout with band
author: Corbet, Eraslan, Lucey, Sensoy
summary: TRB: buy when price exceeds the n-period max by a band, sell when below the n-period min by a band; weaker than VMA in the high-frequency BTC test.
notes: Original on 1-minute data with n-minute holding; translated to daily bars and held until the opposite break.

name: Masuku-Gopane fixed-length MA crossover with band
author: Khumbulani Masuku, Thabo Gopane
summary: FMA rule: buy when the short MA crosses above the long MA by a band, hold ten days; buy signals significantly beat buy-and-hold on BTC/AUD, EUR, JPY, and BTC shows a momentum effect.
notes: Paper holds exactly 10 days after each crossover (no time-exit in vocabulary); exit at the reverse cross instead. 24 rules: short 1,2,5; long 20,50,150,200; band 0/1%. Best cited (2,50,1%).

name: Overreaction inertia (momentum) day trade
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: After a day whose return exceeds the 30-day mean by more than k standard deviations, trade in the same direction the next day; profitable each year 2015-2017 on BTC but not significantly different from random.
long_entry: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
long_exit: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
short_entry: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
short_exit: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
notes: Paper enters at next open and exits same-day close (one-day hold); daily close-to-close here. k=1 chosen as most appropriate in the paper. Paper's overreaction uses open-close returns.

name: Overreaction counter-move (contrarian) day trade
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: Fade a day whose return is more than k standard deviations from the 30-day mean, for one day; found unprofitable on BTC 2015-2017.
long_entry: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
long_exit: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
short_entry: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
short_exit: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) + k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
notes: Included as the short-term reversal counterpart; source reports it as a losing strategy.

name: Decade of crypto trend: EMA crossover (30/40 day)
author: Rozario, Holt, West, Ng
summary: EMA crossover variant from the same study; best in-sample BTC pair 721/951 hours (about 30/40 days) with Sharpe 1.35.
notes: Hourly in the paper; converted to days. In-sample optimised, so expect overfitting.

name: DEMA crossover on Bitcoin (Mo, Wang, Zhang, Huang)
author: Nam Nguyen (summarising Mo, Wang, Zhang, Huang 2025)
summary: Double-EMA crossover with short 1-20 and long 21-50 day windows; BTC DEMA strategy showed relatively stable Sharpe ratios, especially in bear markets.
long_entry: 2 * ema(close, s) - ema(ema(close, s), s) > 2 * ema(close, l) - ema(ema(close, l), l)
long_exit: 2 * ema(close, s) - ema(ema(close, s), s) < 2 * ema(close, l) - ema(ema(close, l), l)
notes: Exact window pairs not given; grid within the stated ranges. SMA and EMA versions of the same test are standard crossovers.

name: Silicon vs Satoshi: QQQ-first Donchian rotation (BTC leg)
author: Cyril Dujava (Quantpedia)
summary: Rotate between QQQ and BTC by Donchian breakout, QQQ checked first, cash otherwise; 20-day variant Calmar 2.25, CAGR 39.5%, MDD -17.6% (2019-2025).
notes: Only the BTC leg is expressible (the QQQ leg is not a BTC/ETH position). Exit rule not explicit in the source; position held only while in breakout. ndx used for QQQ.

name: Dual momentum Bitcoin vs physical gold
author: Cyril Dujava (Quantpedia)
summary: Weekly: hold the better of BTC or GLD over X weeks if its return is positive, else cash; 8-week version 79.9% p.a., Sharpe 1.64 (2018-2026).
notes: Needs a gold price series, which is outside the vocabulary. Lookbacks 1-28 weeks; composite 4/8/12 weeks; optional 20% vol cap.

name: Bitcoin pre-holiday drift with local-high momentum filter
author: Cyril Dujava (Quantpedia)
summary: Within D-5..D+5 of a US public holiday, buy BTC at the close of a day that closes above the prior N-day high (N=5,10,20) and hold one day; Sharpe > 0.6.
notes: Requires a US holiday calendar, not in the vocabulary. Momentum part alone is close > highest(close, N, 1) with one-day hold.

name: Multi-timeframe MACD trend on Bitcoin (D1 filter, H1 entry)
author: David Mesicek (Quantpedia)
summary: Daily MACD(12,26,9) above signal defines uptrend; enter long on hourly MACD up-cross only in daily uptrends, exit on first down hourly bar; Sharpe 1.07 vs 0.33 for plain hourly MACD.
notes: Entries and exits are on 1-hour bars; daily-only framework cannot express it.

name: Fama-Blume x% filter TSMOM on crypto (long/short)
author: Nick Wisselink (Erasmus MSc thesis)
summary: Fama-Blume filter: go long after a rise of x% from a subsequent low, flip short after a fall of x% from a subsequent high; long-only versions earned significant excess returns on crypto portfolios, long-short did not.
notes: Thesis filters 0.5%-20%, reference high/low since last signal (path dependent); approximated with rolling n-day extremes. Equal-weight daily rebalanced coin portfolio; here BTC+ETH.

name: PPO(12,26,9) signal-line crossover on crypto
author: Nick Wisselink (Erasmus MSc thesis)
summary: Percentage price oscillator (MACD normalised by the slow EMA) crossing its 9-day EMA signal line; one of three TSMOM rule families tested on daily crypto 2013-2018.
notes: Long-only variant (the thesis found long-only portfolios significant, long-short not). PPO(12,26,0) zero-line version equals the MACD zero-line rule (see mom-gerritsen-macd-zero).

name: Simple TSMOM 1/7/31-day on crypto (long-only)
author: Nick Wisselink (Erasmus MSc thesis)
summary: Levine-Pedersen simple TSMOM with short crypto formation periods of 1, 7 and 31 days; long when the price is above its level d days ago.
notes: Same rule family as the MOP sign rule but with the thesis's crypto horizons and long-only, equal-weight BTC+ETH.

name: Rohrbach-Suremann-Osterrieder three EMA-pair momentum
author: Janick Rohrbach, Silvan Suremann, Joerg Osterrieder
summary: Momentum signal from three fast/slow EMA pairs (short, intermediate, long horizons), vol-normalised and averaged; on 7 cryptos the time-series version had Sharpe 1.62 and ~-40% max drawdown (gross).
long_entry: ((ema(close, 8) > ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 16) > ema(close, 48))) | ((ema(close, 8) > ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 32) > ema(close, 96))) | ((ema(close, 16) > ema(close, 48)) & (ema(close, 32) > ema(close, 96)))
long_exit: ((ema(close, 8) < ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 16) < ema(close, 48))) | ((ema(close, 8) < ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 32) < ema(close, 96))) | ((ema(close, 16) < ema(close, 48)) & (ema(close, 32) < ema(close, 96)))
short_entry: ((ema(close, 8) < ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 16) < ema(close, 48))) | ((ema(close, 8) < ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 32) < ema(close, 96))) | ((ema(close, 16) < ema(close, 48)) & (ema(close, 32) < ema(close, 96)))
short_exit: ((ema(close, 8) > ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 16) > ema(close, 48))) | ((ema(close, 8) > ema(close, 24)) & (ema(close, 32) > ema(close, 96))) | ((ema(close, 16) > ema(close, 48)) & (ema(close, 32) > ema(close, 96)))
notes: EMA pairs (8,24), (16,48), (32,96) as in the Baz et al. CTA momentum signal the paper builds on; the continuous vol-normalised signal is replaced by a 2-of-3 vote. Earlier SSRN title: 'Momentum in Traditional and Cryptocurrencies Made Simple'.

name: 12M return vs its moving average (TradingView)
author: rahul_joshi_2
summary: Antonacci-inspired: go long when the 12-month return crosses above its own moving average, exit (or short) when it crosses below.
notes: Script default 252 bars on daily, MA length 12; shorting optional and off here. Not BTC-specific in the source.

name: Majors Rotation System (BTC/ETH/SOL/cash)
author: BackQuant
summary: Relative-strength ratio matrix ranks BTC, ETH and SOL and holds the strongest, with a TOTAL-market-cap trend regime filter moving to cash in downtrends.
notes: Invite-only, proprietary scoring indicators; needs SOL and TOTAL market cap. See mom-dual-btc-eth-* for an expressible BTC/ETH relative-momentum switch.

name: High-frequency BTC trend ensemble (Monday Asia open effect)
author: Alberto Pagani (Concretum Group)
summary: Long-short ensemble of intraday trend models on BTC, 20% vol target, gross Sharpe ~1.6 2018-2025; returns concentrated from Sunday 7pm NY for ~24h.
notes: Intraday models with undisclosed rules; daily bars cannot express them.

name: Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum (first half-hour predicts last)
author: Dehua Shen, Andrew Urquhart, Pengfei Wang
summary: Using volume-defined sessions, the first half-hour BTC return positively predicts the last half-hour return; market-timing gains strongest in high-volume/volatility sessions and downturns.
notes: Requires 30-minute intraday data. Financial Review 57(2).

name: Crypto momentum to 2 weeks, reversal after 4 weeks
author: Victoria Dobrynskaya
summary: Cross-sectional: top-30% minus bottom-30% past-return coins earn ~70% p.a. with 2-week ranking/holding; from ~4 weeks the effect reverses up to 2 years.
notes: Cross-sectional across ~2000 coins (Journal of Alternative Investments 26(1)); not a single-asset rule. Informs short lookbacks (<=14d) for BTC/ETH time-series rules.

name: Short-term J/K crypto momentum portfolios
author: Panagiotis Tzouvanas, Renatas Kizys, Bayasgalan Tsend-Ayush
summary: Classic J/K momentum on 12 cryptocurrencies is highly significant for short-term portfolios but disappears longer term; momentum portfolios diversify and hedge traditional assets.
notes: Cross-sectional winner/loser portfolios (Economics Letters 191); J and K not in the abstract.

name: Dynamic time-series momentum periods
author: Oliver Borgards
summary: A dynamic model defines momentum periods following formation periods at daily and intraday frequencies; 20 cryptos show larger and longer momentum periods than US stocks.
notes: Momentum periods are identified by a dynamic segmentation model, not a fixed rule. NAJEF 57.

name: High momentum: distance from k-week high
author: Milan Ficura
summary: Closeness of last week's close to its k-week high positively predicts returns for large liquid coins (t=4.9) while small illiquid coins reverse; large coins show weekly momentum, not reversal.
notes: Paper is a cross-sectional predictive regression; translated for BTC (a large, liquid coin) as a nearness-to-high threshold. Thresholds are my defaults, not from the paper.

name: Crypto momentum factor (CMOM)
author: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski, Xi Wu
summary: Market, size and momentum factors price the cross-section of crypto returns; momentum factor = long past-week winners minus losers.
notes: Cross-sectional factor across many coins (Journal of Finance 2022); no single-asset rule.

name: Crypto-momentum premium (Cryptocurrency as an investable asset class)
author: Nicola Borri, Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski, Xi Wu
summary: Survey-style evidence that cross-sectional crypto-momentum earns persistent excess returns once liquidity, costs and survivorship are handled.
notes: Cross-sectional; horizons not specified in the Quantpedia summary.

name: Multi-horizon EMA time-series momentum on 8 coins
author: Adedeji Daniel Gbadebo
summary: Short/long EMA time-series momentum with volatility normalisation on BTC, ETH and six other coins 2020-2025: 31.96% annual return, beating cross-sectional momentum (55% max drawdown).
notes: EMA spans and vol normalisation not given in the abstract; standard spans assumed. Vol-normalised sizing not expressible.

name: AdaptiveTrend: ROC threshold with ATR trailing stop
author: Duc Bui, Thanh Nguyen
summary: Long when L-period momentum exceeds a threshold, exit on a ratcheting ATR trailing stop (alpha ~2.5); monthly re-optimised over 150+ pairs, Sharpe 2.41 out of sample 2022-2024.
notes: Original on 6-hour bars with monthly grid-search of L, theta, alpha and Sharpe-based asset selection; chandelier-style stop approximates the ratcheting stop. L and theta values not disclosed; defaults mine.

name: Bitcoin rate-of-change with asymmetric thresholds
author: Ayrat Murtazin
summary: Long BTC when the n-day ROC exceeds a buy threshold, sell when it drops below a negative sell threshold; Bayesian-optimised (n=27, +0.1%, -2.72%) but lagged buy-and-hold out of sample.
notes: Thresholds are in percent (ta library ROC). Test 2023-07 to 2024-12: +167.6% vs +215.6% buy-and-hold.

name: Long-term ROC trend (252 and 126 day both positive)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Long-term trend is up when both the 252-day and 126-day ROC are positive; zero-line crossovers identify trend.
notes: Generic equity guidance applied to BTC; exit when both turn negative (between = hold) is my reading.

name: Pring Know Sure Thing signal-line crossover
author: Martin Pring (via StockCharts ChartSchool)
summary: KST = weighted sum of smoothed 10/15/20/30-day ROCs; Pring prefers buying when KST crosses above its 9-day SMA signal line.
long_entry: (sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)) > sma((sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)), 9)
long_exit: (sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)) < sma((sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)), 9)
notes: Daily defaults KST(10,15,20,30,10,10,10,15,9). Generic, not crypto-specific.

name: Coppock curve zero-line cross
author: Edwin Coppock (via StockCharts ChartSchool)
summary: Buy when the WMA of the sum of the 14- and 11-period ROC crosses above zero, sell when it crosses below.
notes: Original on monthly bars (14, 11, 10 months); daily equivalents ~294/231/210 days given as alternatives. Coppock used buy signals only.

name: TRIX(15,9) signal-line crossover
author: Jack Hutson (via StockCharts ChartSchool)
summary: TRIX = 1-day percent change of a triple-smoothed EMA; bullish when TRIX crosses above its 9-day EMA signal line.
long_entry: roc(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1) > ema(roc(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1), 9)
long_exit: roc(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1) < ema(roc(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1), 9)
notes: Default 15; generic oscillator rule applied to BTC.

name: RSI + volume surge momentum breakout
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Enter when RSI crosses above 50 with volume above 1.5x its 20-day average; exit when RSI falls below 45; claimed Sharpe 1.87 on BTC 2024-2025.
notes: RSI length not stated (14 assumed); bearish-divergence exit omitted. Figures unverified and not linked to a backtest.

name: MACD histogram expansion + EMA50 trend filter
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Enter when the MACD histogram has expanded 3+ bars and price is above the 50 EMA; claimed Sharpe 1.62 on ETH 2024-2025.
long_entry: (macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9) > shift(macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9), 1)) & (shift(macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9), 1) > shift(macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9), 2)) & (shift(macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9), 2) > shift(macd(close, 12, 26) - macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9), 3)) & (macd(close, 12, 26) > macd_signal(close, 12, 26, 9)) & (close > ema(close, 50))
notes: Exit not specified in source; histogram turning negative or price below EMA50 assumed. Figures unverified.

name: Order-flow imbalance (CVD) + RSI momentum
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Enter when RSI > 52 and cumulative volume delta has risen for 3+ periods; claimed Sharpe 2.26 on BTC 2024-2025.
notes: CVD rising approximated by taker-buy share > 50% three days running; exit not specified (assumed). Figures unverified.

name: On-chain activity + price momentum
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: RSI above 55 plus BTC active addresses up >15% week over week; claimed Sharpe 2.18.
notes: Needs active-address on-chain data.

name: Whale activity + momentum confluence
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: RSI > 52, MACD positive, >$1M transactions up 40% vs 7-day average and net exchange outflows.
notes: Needs on-chain transaction and exchange-flow data.

name: Social-sentiment-filtered momentum
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: RSI crosses above 55, volume >120% of 20-day average, and social sentiment score up >30% in 24h; claimed Sharpe 1.94 on ETH.
notes: Needs a social sentiment feed.

name: Grobys-Ahmed-Sapkota 20-day variable moving average
author: Grobys, Ahmed, Sapkota
summary: VMA rule on 11 major cryptocurrencies 2016-2018: buy when price is above its 20-day MA, sell when below; the 20-day rule earned ~8.76% p.a. excess return (excluding Bitcoin), implying inefficiency.
notes: VMA classifies every day as buy or sell, so expressed long/short; the result excluded BTC, so ETH is the asset here. Finance Research Letters 32.

name: ETH buy after negative abnormal day (contrarian exception)
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: Exception to next-day momentum: ETH shows a contrarian (rebound) effect after negative abnormal-return days; buy for one day after an abnormally negative day.
long_entry: roc(close, 1) < sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
long_exit: roc(close, 1) > sma(roc(close, 1), n) - k * stdev(roc(close, 1), n)
notes: One-day hold; companion to mom-caporale-plastun-eth-abnormal-up and the BTC entries.

name: Bitcoin MIN: buy at n-day low (mean reversion leg)
author: Matus Padysak, Radovan Vojtko
summary: Hold BTC the day after it closes at its n-day minimum; lower returns than MAX but much less risky than buying above the minimum; weak in the 2022-2024 revisit.
notes: Reversal counterpart to the MAX momentum rule; included for the momentum-vs-reversal comparison.

name: Alpha Architect trend score (TMOM + 12-month MA)
author: Alpha Architect
summary: Two signals: time-series momentum versus cash and price versus its 12-month moving average; score 100 when both positive, 50 when one, 0 when none.
long_entry: (close > shift(close, n) * (1 + us2y / 100 * n / 365)) & (close > sma(close, n))
long_exit: (close <= shift(close, n) * (1 + us2y / 100 * n / 365)) & (close <= sma(close, n))
notes: Full long only when both signals agree, flat when both negative, hold in between (approximates the 50% state). TMOM window not stated; 12 months assumed. us2y proxies cash. Generic, not crypto-specific.

name: Trend quantification with four PPOs (20/40/60/80 vs 150)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Four PPOs with a fixed 150-day slow EMA and fast EMAs of 20/40/60/80 days; each positive PPO adds 25% exposure, fully invested when all four are positive.
notes: Each parameter value is one 25% sleeve; run all four (20/40/60/80) equal-weight to reproduce the scaling. Generic, not crypto-specific.

name: Moving Momentum (20/150 SMA bias + stochastic pullback + MACD histogram)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: In an uptrend (20-day SMA above 150-day SMA), buy when the stochastic has dipped below 20 and the MACD histogram turns positive; mirror for shorts.
notes: 'Stochastic dipped below 20 then histogram turned positive' approximated by a 10-day lookback on the stochastic. Exit rule is my reading (opposite setup or trend flip).

name: Daily momentum in the largest coins (vs reversal in small coins)
author: Zaremba, Bilgin, Long, Mercik, Szczygielski
summary: Crypto shows strong cross-sectional daily reversal driven by illiquid coins, but the handful of largest, most tradeable coins exhibit daily momentum instead.
notes: Cross-sectional sorts. For BTC/ETH the implication is next-day continuation; see mom-liu-tsyvinski-daily-tsmom (n=1) for the time-series rule.

name: MAX momentum in cryptocurrencies
author: Li, Urquhart, Wang, Zhang
summary: Unlike stocks, coins with the highest maximum daily return over the past month earn higher future returns ('MAX momentum'), robust to longer holding periods.
notes: Cross-sectional sort on maximum daily return; no single-asset rule.

name: VIX premium predicts crypto momentum
author: Chang, Nie, Chang, Cheng, Yen
summary: A higher VIX premium (VIX minus realised volatility) forecasts a larger crypto momentum premium one month ahead; VIX level and EPU do not.
notes: Conditions a cross-sectional momentum portfolio; a time-series BTC version would be invented, so left unexpressed.

name: Short-term contrarian beats momentum in top-100 coins
author: Koscielny (Kosc), Sakowski, Slepaczuk
summary: Across the 100 largest coins, short-term contrarian portfolios clearly dominate momentum and benchmarks (including BTC buy-and-hold), depending on reallocation period and ranking window.
notes: Cross-sectional ranking portfolios (Physica A 523).

name: High-frequency EMA momentum on 7 large coins
author: Chu, Chan, Zhang
summary: Signal-based (EMA) high-frequency momentum strategies on the seven largest cryptocurrencies earn abnormal returns versus passive portfolios; no single parameterisation dominates.
notes: Intraday sampling; parameters not in abstract.

name: Random-forest forecasting of Bitcoin with technical indicators
author: Gradojevic et al.
summary: Trend, momentum, volume and sentiment indicators fed to nonlinear models beat a random walk for daily BTC (random forest best); drivers shifted from trend-following to momentum and sentiment.
notes: Machine-learning model output, not a rule.

name: Cryptocurrency factor momentum
author: Fieberg, Liedtke, Metko, Zaremba
summary: Across 34 crypto anomalies, past winning factors outperform past losers; unlike stocks, crypto factor momentum originates from price momentum.
notes: Factor-level cross-sectional strategy.

name: Intraday momentum and reversal in Bitcoin
author: Zhuzhu Wen, Elie Bouri, Yahua Xu, Yang Zhao
summary: Intraday BTC returns show both momentum (late-informed traders) and reversal (overreaction); a timing strategy on intraday predictors beats always-long; also in ETH, LTC, XRP.
notes: Needs intraday half-hour returns.

name: Simple technical rules selected out of 75,360 (bitcoin)
author: Niek Deprez, Michael Frommel
summary: From 75,360 rules in six classes at daily and intraday frequency, cost-adjusted multiple-testing selection and rule portfolios beat buy-and-hold out of sample on a risk-adjusted basis.
notes: Selected rule portfolio is not disclosed in the abstract; rule classes not named.

name: 69 MA and breakout rules under costs and bubbles
author: Svogun, Bazan-Palomino
summary: MA and breakout rules on BTC, ETH, XRP, LTC, BCH (daily and 1-minute, 2016-2021): bubbles help ETH/XRP/LTC rules beat buy-and-hold; transaction costs oddly raise the chance for BTC and ETH.
notes: Specific rule parameters not in the abstract; see the MA/TRB entries from Gerritsen and Corbet for the rule shapes.

name: Momentum or reversal as the third crypto factor
author: Jia, Goodell, Shen
summary: Tests whether a momentum or a reversal factor better completes crypto asset-pricing models.
notes: Factor-model study, cross-sectional.

name: Risk preferences and crypto momentum
author: Proelss, Schweizer, Buchwalter
summary: Studies whether investor risk preferences drive the crypto momentum premium.
notes: Cross-sectional, explanatory study.

name: Expert-ranked EMA/RSI/Ichimoku/MACD rules on BTC and ETH
author: Milad Abbasi, Somayeh Mousavi, Abbasali Jafari Nodoushan
summary: Fuzzy-TOPSIS expert ranking picked EMA, RSI, Ichimoku and MACD; grid-search/PSO-optimised and combined rules beat buy-and-hold on BTC and ETH 2018-2020.
notes: Exact entry/exit definitions and optimised parameters are not in the abstract.

name: Fear & Greed-gated momentum
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Act on momentum signals only when the Crypto Fear & Greed Index is 20-40, skip at 75-90; claimed Sharpe 2.07 on BTC 2023-2025.
notes: Underlying momentum entry not defined in the source (fear_greed is available, but the trigger is missing).

name: DCA + momentum hybrid
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Weekly DCA that doubles when RSI > 55 with rising volume and skips when RSI < 40; claimed +198% vs +156% plain DCA.
notes: Accumulation schedule, not a position rule.

name: Multi-timeframe RSI alignment (15m/1h/4h)
author: LedgerMind Research
summary: Enter when RSI is above 50 on 15-minute, 1-hour and 4-hour charts simultaneously; claimed 87% win rate.
notes: Intraday timeframes.

name: Multi-Horizon Momentum Curve (vol-normalised 5/10/20/40)
author: BackQuant
summary: Momentum over 5/10/20/40 bars, each divided by one-bar return volatility times sqrt(N), weighted toward longer horizons and combined; bullish above +threshold, bearish below -threshold.
long_entry: (1 * roc(close, 5) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 2.236) + 2 * roc(close, 10) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 3.162) + 3 * roc(close, 20) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 4.472) + 4 * roc(close, 40) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 6.325)) / 10 > th
long_exit: (1 * roc(close, 5) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 2.236) + 2 * roc(close, 10) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 3.162) + 3 * roc(close, 20) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 4.472) + 4 * roc(close, 40) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 6.325)) / 10 < 0 - th
short_entry: (1 * roc(close, 5) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 2.236) + 2 * roc(close, 10) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 3.162) + 3 * roc(close, 20) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 4.472) + 4 * roc(close, 40) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 6.325)) / 10 < 0 - th
short_exit: (1 * roc(close, 5) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 2.236) + 2 * roc(close, 10) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 3.162) + 3 * roc(close, 20) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 4.472) + 4 * roc(close, 40) / (stdev(roc(close, 1), v) * 6.325)) / 10 > th
notes: Weights 1-4 and volatility window are my assumptions (page says weights increase with horizon, defaults not listed); simple ROC replaces log returns; clamp and EMA smoothing omitted. Indicator, not a strategy, in the source.

name: Bitcoin Sniper Confluence (EMA 9/21 with BTC gates)
author: viprasol
summary: EMA 9/21 crossover counts only when an 8-factor confluence score (min 5) agrees and BTC gates (macro link to NQ/DXY, session windows, weekend block, ADR exhaustion) are open.
notes: Needs BTC dominance, intraday session windows and hidden confluence factors.

name: Gaussian Channel + StochRSI BTC momentum continuation
author: cs_lev
summary: Daily BTC strategy capturing momentum continuation with a Gaussian channel and a stochastic-RSI filter.
notes: Gaussian filter channel is not in the vocabulary and rules are not described on the page.

name: Log-price moving-average (PMA) ratio
author: Mingzhe Wei (Glasgow PhD thesis)
summary: Proposes a log-price MA ratio that keeps significant forecasting power for crypto returns after Lucky-Factors data-snooping control, whereas plain MA rule profits may be data-snooped.
notes: Requires a log transform not in the vocabulary; exact construction not in the abstract.

name: Google-search attention predicts Bitcoin returns
author: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Top-quintile weekly Google searches for 'Bitcoin' were followed by 11.2% next-week returns vs 1.1% for the bottom quintile; 'Bitcoin hack' searches predict lower returns.
notes: Needs Google Trends data.

name: Frequency of daily abnormal returns predicts Bitcoin
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun, Viktor Oliinyk
summary: The difference between the frequency of positive and negative abnormal-return days over a window predicts BTC returns (piecewise-linear and consensus models best, 2013-2020).
notes: Regression model on counts of abnormal days; counting booleans over a window is not supported by the vocabulary, and no explicit trading rule is given.
